material_systems.name: Solvent-Based MDF Edge Sealer

primer.notes: MUST be applied to MDF cut/routed edges BEFORE any latex product. Water-based primers cause irreversible fiber swelling on MDF edges. Step 1 of two-step MDF prime. Overhead application requires careful technique — sealer tends to run/drip from overhead edges due to gravity. Apply in thin coats.

material_systems.notes: Edge-only application. Step 1 of MDF two-step prime process. Overhead edge sealing is more difficult than wall edge sealing — gravity pulls sealer away from overhead edges.

material_systems.name: High-Build Latex Face Primer for MDF

primer.notes: Applied to MDF face surfaces AFTER edge sealing with shellac/oil-based. Builds film, levels surface. Step 2 of two-step MDF prime. Overhead application — monitor for sags on horizontal surfaces.

material_systems.notes: Step 2 of MDF two-step prime. Face surfaces only — edges already sealed.

material_systems.name: Stain-Blocking Primer for FJP/Poplar

products: Benjamin Moore Fresh Start Oil-Based Primer
primer.notes: MANDATORY for bare FJP. Resin and green mineral streaks bleed through standard latex primers without stain-blocking. NOT optional. Per Millwork_NC_Paint_Doctrine §2.2 and §4.1.

material_systems.notes: Substrate-driven. Stain-blocking is not optional for FJP ceiling panels/boards.

material_systems.name: Tannin-Blocking Primer for Hardwood

primer.notes: Blocks tannin bleed-through on bare hardwood (oak, cherry, walnut, maple). Per Millwork Doctrine §4.

material_systems.notes: Substrate-driven. Required for all bare hardwood wood ceiling substrates.

primer.notes: Standard primer-sealer for bare softwood ceiling panels/boards.

material_systems.name: Standard Acrylic Trim Enamel

products: Sherwin-Williams ProClassic Waterborne Interior Acrylic Enamel
Benjamin Moore Regal Select Interior Semi-Gloss
finish.notes: Fast dry/recoat. Non-yellowing. Water cleanup. Overhead application — apply lighter coats to prevent sags on horizontal ceiling surfaces. Same system as trim, window, riser, wainscot, and wood wall specs.

material_systems.notes: QT3 — satin is the only sheen per sheen/QT gate (FFD §4.1). Material systems are recommendations — contractor has discretion (RC-005).

material_systems.name: Modified Urethane Trim Enamel

products: Benjamin Moore Advance Waterborne Interior Alkyd
Sherwin-Williams Pro Industrial Waterbased Alkyd Urethane
finish.notes: Superior flow and leveling. SHORT working time — apply, tip once, walk away (FFD §15.3.1). Overhead application amplifies open-time concern — warm air at ceiling level accelerates dry time, reducing working window. Apply in manageable sections. Same system as all other fine finish specs.

material_systems.notes: QT4. Material systems are recommendations — contractor has discretion (RC-005).

material_systems.name: Premium Urethane Trim Enamel

finish.coat_notes: QT5 brush typically requires 3+ coats per FFD §15.10.3.
finish.notes: Maximum durability. Excellent leveling. Emerald Urethane is acrylic-urethane enamel, NOT waterborne alkyd (RC-006). Same system as all other fine finish specs.

material_systems.notes: QT5. Gloss available only at this tier. Material systems are recommendations — contractor has discretion (RC-005).

coverage_profiles.notes: Wood ceiling panel/board primer coverage. SF measured directly from PaintScope input. Coffered style beam faces add ~15% effective surface area over measured ceiling SF. Beadboard/T&G groove detail adds ~5-10% effective surface area. Overhead spray application may have slightly higher waste factor due to gravity-related material loss.
assumptions: Single coat primer system (except MDF two-step: edge seal + face prime)
Wood ceiling SF from PaintScope input PS_SURFACE_SF.WOOD_CEILING

coverage_profiles.notes: Wood ceiling panel/board finish coat coverage on primed smooth surface. Two-coat standard; third coat at QT5 brush. Coffered style may consume ~15% more material due to beam face surface area. Beadboard/T&G groove detail increases consumption ~5-10%. Spray method: add 20-30% waste for overhead overspray.
assumptions: Wood ceiling SF from PaintScope input
Coffered beam faces add ~15% to effective surface area
Beadboard/T&G groove detail adds ~5-10% to effective surface area

consumables.name: Canvas drop cloth
consumables.usage: Full floor protection below ceiling work zone (spray) or perimeter runners (brush)
consumables.notes: Spray: full room floor coverage — overspray from overhead falls onto entire floor. Much more material than wood wall (which only needs perimeter drops). Brush: perimeter runners along work path for drip protection.

consumables.name: Rosin paper (builder's paper)
consumables.usage: Full floor protection below ceiling work zone (spray)
consumables.notes: Alternative to canvas drop cloths for full floor coverage during spray. 500 SF per roll. Tape seams to prevent gaps. Full room coverage required for overhead ceiling spray.

consumables.name: Masking tape (1.5" blue painter's tape)
consumables.usage: Wall upper band masking, fixture masking, general edge masking
consumables.notes: 60 yards = 180 LF per roll. Wall upper band masking at ceiling-wall junction (spray only). Fixture masking (always). Tape line at wall-ceiling junction — paper/film hangs down from tape edge.

consumables.name: Masking paper (12-inch)
consumables.usage: Wall upper band surface masking at ceiling-wall junction (spray only)
consumables.notes: Paper + tape system for wall surface protection at ceiling-wall junction during overhead spray. 12-inch width covers upper wall band. Inverse of wood wall's ceiling_line masking — here we mask the wall BELOW the ceiling.

consumables.name: Pre-taped masking film
consumables.usage: Extended wall upper band masking when wall is finished (spray only)
consumables.notes: Pre-taped plastic film for wider wall coverage when finished wall surface needs full protection from ceiling overspray. 24-inch or wider film. Alternative to masking paper for finished walls.

consumables.name: Plastic sheeting (lightweight)
consumables.usage: Opening covers for windows/doors during spray, fixture bags
consumables.notes: Lightweight plastic for quick pin-up over window/door openings to catch overspray fallout. Also used for fixture bagging. Spray only.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 150-grit
consumables.usage: Pre-primer sanding for bare substrates, factory primer scuff
consumables.notes: 150 grit for initial bare wood sanding and factory primer scuff. ALL sanding is overhead — pole sander strongly recommended for field areas to reduce fatigue.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 220-grit
consumables.usage: Pre-primer final sand, between-coat sanding (QT3 spot, QT4 full)
consumables.notes: 220 grit for final prep sand and between-coat sanding. Rigid sanding block mandatory (FFD §15.4.1). Flexible sanding sponge for beadboard/T&G grooves and coffered beam-panel inside corners. Overhead sanding generates dust that falls onto worker — PPE required.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 320-grit
consumables.notes: 220-320 grit range at QT5. Uniform scratch pattern required.

consumables.name: Sanding block (fine grit range)
consumables.usage: Rigid block for between-coat sanding. Mandatory per FFD §15.4.1.
consumables.notes: One block per crew, reusable. Rigid block critical for flat plank and coffered panel field surfaces.

consumables.name: Sanding sponge (fine grit range)
consumables.usage: Flexible sanding for beadboard/T&G grooves and coffered beam-panel inside corners
consumables.notes: Flexible sanding sponge conforms to groove profiles and inside corners where rigid block cannot reach. Essential for beadboard (high groove density) and coffered (beam-panel inside corners).

consumables.name: Angled sash brush (2-2.5")
consumables.usage: Primary brush for wood ceiling panel faces, beam detail (coffered), and cutting-in
consumables.notes: 2-2.5 inch for flat plank faces, board faces, and coffered beam detail. One per painter per material change.

consumables.name: Airless spray tip 310-411
consumables.usage: Fine atomization for wood ceiling panel/board spray finish
consumables.notes: Tight fan pattern for wood ceiling work. Board styles: sweep passes following board direction overhead. Coffered: field panels first (broad overhead passes), then beam faces. Lighter coats overhead to prevent sags.

consumables.name: Tack cloth
consumables.usage: Remove sanding dust before each coat application
consumables.notes: One tack cloth covers ~30 SF of wood ceiling surface. Use before every coat. Overhead tacking — work tack cloth into beadboard/T&G grooves and coffered beam-panel corners.

consumables.name: Paintable acrylic latex caulk
consumables.usage: Board/panel joints, beam-panel junctions (coffered), and perimeter at ceiling-wall junction
consumables.notes: Joint types vary by ceiling_style: (1) Board styles (beadboard, T&G, flat_plank) — board-to-board joints. Beadboard has highest joint density. (2) Coffered — beam-to-panel junctions (inside corners), beam-to-beam joints. (3) ALL styles — perimeter caulk at ceiling-to-wall junction. Use thicker-consistency caulk for overhead — gravity pulls thin caulk from joints.

consumables.name: Lightweight spackle compound
consumables.usage: Fill fastener holes on wood ceiling panels/boards
consumables.notes: ELEVATED CONSUMPTION on board-style ceilings (beadboard, T&G, flat_plank). Each board is face-nailed at every joist. Overhead spackle application is messier — spackle drips from putty knife. Use thicker-consistency lightweight spackle for overhead work. Overfill-sand-flush method with HIGH waste factor.

consumables.name: Sandable wood filler
consumables.usage: Fill deeper defects, damaged board/panel edges, and knot holes
consumables.notes: Supplement to spackle for deeper fills. One quart per ~100 SF of wood ceiling assembly.

floor_full.description: Full floor coverage below ceiling work zone for overhead spray overspray

floor_perimeter.description: Perimeter drop cloth runners for brush drip protection

wall_upper_band.description: Paper/film masking at ceiling-wall junction to protect finished wall from overspray

fixture_covers.description: Ceiling-mounted fixture masking (lights, fans, smoke detectors, sprinkler heads)
fixture_covers.condition: ALWAYS — fixtures are embedded in the ceiling work surface

opening_cover_lightweight.description: Lightweight plastic pin-up over window/door openings for overhead spray overspray fallout

required_inputs.purpose: Wall upper band masking SF (spray only)

compatibility_rules.description: All finish systems are compatible with all primer systems
compatibility_rules.notes: Primer and finish are independent selections. All combinations valid.

compatibility_rules.description: SS_PRIMED_FACTORY compatible with all finish systems
compatibility_rules.notes: Scuff sand factory primer for adhesion. No additional primer needed.

compatibility_rules.description: MDF two-step prime: shellac edge seal MUST precede latex face prime
compatibility_rules.notes: SYS_PRIMER_MDF_SHELLAC on edges first, then SYS_PRIMER_MDF_LATEX on faces. Never reverse.

risk_notes.topic: MDF fiber swelling on routed edges
risk_notes.risk: Irreversible fiber swelling if water-based product contacts raw MDF cut/routed edges
risk_notes.mitigation: Always seal MDF edges with shellac/oil-based sealer (SYS_PRIMER_MDF_SHELLAC) before any latex product.

risk_notes.risk: Resin and green mineral streaks bleed through non-stain-blocking primer on bare FJP
risk_notes.mitigation: Use SYS_PRIMER_POPLAR_STAINBLOCK. Stain-blocking is MANDATORY for bare FJP.

risk_notes.risk: Tannin bleed re-emerges through multiple finish coats on bare hardwood
risk_notes.mitigation: Use SYS_PRIMER_HARDWOOD_TANNINBLOCK. Required for all bare hardwood substrates.

risk_notes.topic: Overhead sags and drips on ceiling surface
risk_notes.risk: Gravity pulls wet coating downward from overhead horizontal surface, creating sags at board edges and drip accumulation at joints and beam corners (coffered)
risk_notes.mitigation: Apply lighter coats overhead than on walls. Multiple thin coats better than one heavy coat. Monitor board edges, joints, and beam-panel junctions for accumulation during application.

risk_notes.topic: Beadboard groove holidays — incomplete coverage in narrow grooves overhead
risk_notes.risk: Spray passes too fast across narrow beadboard grooves, brush too wide for groove detail. Overhead angle makes groove bottoms harder to reach.
risk_notes.mitigation: Angle spray passes to reach groove bottoms. Size brush to groove width. Check all grooves for holidays before moving on. Use angled light for overhead inspection.

risk_notes.risk: Incomplete coverage in inside corners where beams meet panels — spray can't reach corners, brush misses recessed areas
risk_notes.mitigation: Panel fields first, then beam faces with HVLP or fine-finish tip. Check all inside corners for holidays. Use angled light for overhead inspection.

risk_notes.topic: Board groove fill — loss of groove definition on beadboard/T&G
risk_notes.risk: Excessive paint buildup in grooves, filling the groove profile. Gravity causes paint to pool in grooves on overhead surfaces.
risk_notes.mitigation: Thin coats on board-style ceilings. Spray preferred — atomized application minimizes groove fill. Extra vigilance overhead where gravity pools material in grooves.

risk_notes.risk: Gravity pulls wet caulk out of overhead joints, creating uneven joint lines
risk_notes.mitigation: Apply caulk in shorter beads overhead. Tool immediately. Use thicker-consistency caulk formulation.

material_notes.dual_system_architecture: TWO independent material system layers: (1) Primer systems are substrate-driven with 5 distinct paths. (2) Finish systems are QT-driven. Identical architecture to SF_WOOD_WALL_NC, SF_WAINSCOT_PANEL_NC.
material_notes.overhead_material_note: Overhead application requires thinner coats to prevent sags. May increase total coat count or material waste. Spray waste factor higher overhead due to gravity-related material loss. Coverage rates similar per-coat but more coats may be needed for full coverage.
material_notes.coffered_material_note: Coffered beams add ~15% effective surface area over measured ceiling SF due to beam faces, soffits, and inside corners. Material consumption higher than flat_plank for the same measured SF.
material_notes.floor_protection_note: Floor protection for spray is FULL room (floor_full zone) unlike wood wall which only needs perimeter. Significantly more protection material consumed. Canvas drop cloths or builder's paper over entire floor below ceiling work zone.
material_notes.product_classification: Advance is waterborne alkyd. Emerald Urethane is acrylic-urethane enamel (RC-006).

assumptions.value: 350-450 SF/gal for finish coat on primed smooth surface
assumptions.source: Manufacturer PDS data, aligned with all fine finish spec coverage

assumptions.value: ~15% more material consumption for coffered due to beam face surface area
assumptions.source: Research estimate U-003 based on typical beam dimensions and grid density
assumptions.note: No doctrine provides coffered ceiling surface area multiplier.

assumptions.value: ~5-10% more material consumption for beadboard/T&G due to paint in groove detail
assumptions.source: Research estimate based on groove dimensions and board width
assumptions.note: Same basis as wood wall shiplap/T&G groove material estimate.
